cases.scenario: Create a new pet with all valid fields
cases.steps:
1. Send POST /pet with a full valid pet payload (unique id generated per run)
2. Check status code
3. Compare response fields (id, name, category, photoUrls, tags, status) with the request payload
cases.expected: HTTP 200; response body echoes the created pet with the same id, name, photoUrls, tags and status
cases.notes: All echoed fields match the payload.

cases.scenario: Created pet can be retrieved by GET /pet/{petId}
cases.expected: HTTP 200; same id and name as the created pet
cases.notes: Verifies the POST actually persisted the record, not only echoed it.

cases.scenario: Create a pet with only the required fields (no category, no tags)
cases.steps:
1. Send POST /pet with id, name and photoUrls only
2. Check status code and echoed fields
cases.expected: HTTP 200; pet is created; category and tags are optional and may be omitted
cases.notes: Optional fields are not required - matches the documented schema.

cases.scenario: Empty payload must be rejected
cases.steps:
1. Send POST /pet with body {}
2. Check that the API rejects the payload (documented: 405 Invalid input)
cases.expected: HTTP 405 Invalid input - name and photoUrls are required fields
cases.notes: Defect: the API accepts an empty payload and creates a nameless record with a generated id (3174071910010089500). See BUG-002.

cases.scenario: Payload without required field "name" must be rejected
cases.steps:
1. Send POST /pet without the required "name" field
2. Check that the API rejects the payload
cases.expected: HTTP 405 Invalid input - "name" is a required field per the schema
cases.notes: Defect: pet is created without a name. See BUG-002. Record was cleaned up afterwards (DELETE).

cases.scenario: Payload without required field "photoUrls" must be rejected
cases.steps:
1. Send POST /pet without the required "photoUrls" field
2. Check that the API rejects the payload
cases.expected: HTTP 405 Invalid input - "photoUrls" is a required field per the schema
cases.notes: Defect: pet is created with photoUrls defaulted to []. See BUG-002. Record was cleaned up afterwards (DELETE).

cases.scenario: Malformed JSON body must be rejected
cases.steps:
1. Send POST /pet with syntactically invalid JSON
2. Check that the API returns an error and does not create a record
cases.expected: HTTP 400; parse error, no pet is created

cases.scenario: Status value outside the documented enum must be rejected
cases.steps:
1. Send POST /pet with status "sleepy" (allowed: available, pending, sold)
2. Check that the API rejects the payload
3. (observed) GET the pet id to see whether the invalid value was persisted
cases.expected: HTTP 405 Invalid input - "status" only allows available, pending, sold
cases.actual: HTTP 200 in 255 ms; body: {"id":311323678,"name":"QA_BadStatus_1792031132367","photoUrls":[],"tags":[],"status":"sleepy"} | GET /pet/311323678 -> HTTP 200, status field: "sleepy"
cases.notes: Defect: invalid status is accepted and persisted. See BUG-002. Record was cleaned up afterwards (DELETE).

cases.scenario: Boundary: 255-character name is stored without truncation
cases.steps:
1. Send POST /pet with a 255-character name
2. Verify the response echoes the full 255-character name
cases.expected: HTTP 200; name is stored and returned in full (no documented length limit)
cases.actual: HTTP 200 in 254 ms; echoed name length: 255 chars
cases.notes: No truncation observed. Record was cleaned up afterwards (DELETE).

cases.scenario: Boundary: negative pet id must be rejected or honored as sent
cases.steps:
1. Send POST /pet with id -1
2. Check the id in the response
3. Try to retrieve the pet using the returned id
cases.expected: HTTP 405 (invalid input) or HTTP 200 with id -1 preserved
cases.notes: Defect: id -1 is silently replaced with 3174071910010089500; the record cannot be retrieved with either the sent id (-1) or the returned id. See BUG-003.

cases.scenario: Find pets by status "available" returns only available pets
cases.steps:
1. Send GET /pet/findByStatus?status=available
2. Check status code and that the body is a JSON array
3. Verify every returned pet has status = "available"
cases.expected: HTTP 200; JSON array where every element has status "available"
cases.actual: HTTP 200 in 819 ms; 686 pets returned, elements with status != available: 0
cases.notes: Array is large (public shared dataset) - full array was parsed and validated in code.

cases.scenario: Find pets by status "pending" (valid status, possibly empty result)
cases.steps:
1. Send GET /pet/findByStatus?status=pending
2. Check status code and body type
3. Verify every returned pet has status = "pending"
cases.expected: HTTP 200; JSON array (may be empty) where every element has status "pending"
cases.actual: HTTP 200 in 254 ms; 0 pets returned, elements with status != pending: 0
cases.notes: Empty result is valid here because the shared dataset currently has no pending pets.

cases.scenario: Find pets by status "sold" returns only sold pets
cases.steps:
1. Send GET /pet/findByStatus?status=sold
2. Check status code and body type
3. Verify every returned pet has status = "sold"
cases.expected: HTTP 200; JSON array where every element has status "sold"
cases.actual: HTTP 200 in 258 ms; 212 pets returned, elements with status != sold: 0

cases.scenario: Multiple status parameters are combined (available + pending)
cases.steps:
1. Send GET /pet/findByStatus?status=available&status=pending
2. Verify the result only contains pets with status available or pending
cases.expected: HTTP 200; JSON array where every element has status "available" or "pending"
cases.actual: HTTP 200 in 550 ms; 686 pets returned, elements outside {available, pending}: 0

cases.scenario: Invalid status value must be rejected with 400
cases.steps:
1. Send GET /pet/findByStatus?status=notastatus
2. Check that the API returns 400 Invalid status value as documented
cases.expected: HTTP 400 Invalid status value
cases.notes: Defect: invalid value is treated as a filter and returns 200 with an empty array instead of 400. See BUG-001.

cases.scenario: Missing required query parameter "status" must be rejected
cases.steps:
1. Send GET /pet/findByStatus without the required status parameter
2. Check that the API returns 400
cases.expected: HTTP 400 (status is a required query parameter)
cases.notes: Defect: missing parameter returns 200 with an empty array, hiding the client mistake. See BUG-001.

cases.scenario: Newly created pet appears in its status list and disappears after deletion
cases.steps:
1. POST /pet with status "pending" (id 311323687)
2. GET /pet/findByStatus?status=pending and confirm the pet is present
3. DELETE /pet/311323687
4. Repeat the search and confirm the pet is gone
cases.expected: Pet is present in the pending list after creation and absent after deletion
cases.actual: POST -> HTTP 200; present in list after create: true; DELETE -> HTTP 200; present after delete: false
cases.notes: Cross-endpoint check: create -> search -> delete -> search.

cases.scenario: Delete an existing pet returns 200 and the deleted id
cases.preconditions: Pet 311323690 exists (created via POST in this run)
cases.expected: HTTP 200; body contains code 200 and message = deleted pet id

cases.scenario: Deleted pet is no longer retrievable by id
cases.steps:
1. After deletion, send GET /pet/{petId} with the deleted id
2. Verify the pet is gone
cases.expected: HTTP 404 "Pet not found"
cases.actual: HTTP 404 in 255 ms; body: {"code":1,"type":"error","message":"Pet not found"}
cases.notes: Confirms the deletion is effective on this endpoint, not just acknowledged.

cases.scenario: Deleted pet no longer appears in findByStatus results
cases.steps:
1. After deletion, search status "available"
2. Confirm the deleted pet id is not in the result
cases.expected: HTTP 200; deleted pet id is absent from the array
cases.actual: HTTP 200 in 272 ms; array size: 686; deleted pet present: false

cases.scenario: Delete a pet that does not exist returns 404
cases.steps:
1. Send DELETE /pet/{petId} with an id that does not exist
2. Check status code
cases.expected: HTTP 404 Pet not found
cases.notes: Status code matches the documentation. Note: for numeric ids the 404 body is empty, while non-numeric ids return a JSON error - inconsistent format (low impact, see API-DELETE-005).

cases.scenario: Non-numeric petId must be rejected with 400 Invalid ID
cases.steps:
1. Send DELETE /pet/abc
2. Check that the API returns 400 Invalid ID supplied as documented
cases.expected: HTTP 400 Invalid ID supplied
cases.actual: HTTP 404 in 255 ms; body: {"code":404,"type":"unknown","message":"java.lang.NumberFormatException: For input string: \"abc\""}
cases.notes: Defect: returns 404 with an internal java.lang.NumberFormatException message instead of 400. See BUG-004.

cases.scenario: Boundary: pet id 0 does not exist
cases.steps:
1. Send DELETE /pet/0
2. Check status code
cases.expected: HTTP 404 Pet not found (id 0 is a valid integer but no such pet exists)
cases.notes: Empty 404 body for numeric ids, same as API-DELETE-004.

cases.scenario: Boundary: DELETE without a petId is not allowed
cases.steps:
1. Send DELETE /pet (no id)
2. Check that the API rejects the request
cases.expected: HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed (no such route)
